# Background
All NPS units in the Cumberland Piedmont Inventory and Monitoring Network (CUPN) take part in a monitoring protocol to track the presence and extent of ozone foliar injury on target plant species. Resource Briefs that summarize findings at each NPS unit in each monitoring year can be found on NPS DataStore under project reference code [2312827](https://irma.nps.gov/DataStore/Reference/Profile/2302031). Here, we show changes in the presence and rate of both suspected and confirmed ozone foliar injury at monitored sites across the monitoring period.

```{r, include=FALSE}
## Load packages
packageNames <- c( "ggplot2", "lubridate", "stringr", "ggpubr", "dplyr", "here","data.table", "remotes", "showtext", "sysfonts", "forcats", "scales", "glmmTMB", "DHARMa", "broom.mixed", "datawizard", "performance", "see", "lmerTest", "purrr", "patchwork", "dotwhisker")

# get names of packages that still need to be installed and install them 
install.packages(packageNames[!(packageNames %in% (installed.packages() |> rownames()))])
 
# now, load all packages
lapply(X = packageNames, FUN = function(x) require(package = x, character.only = TRUE))

## set global options
ggplot2::set_theme(theme_classic())

## load foliar injury data
datAll <- read.csv("../Data/2315044/CUPN_OzoneFoliarInjury_SpeciesAssesment.csv")
datAll <- datAll |> 
  mutate(startDate = as_date(startDate)) |> # format the date
  mutate(year = year(startDate)) |> # make a column for year
  mutate(damageAmountCode_bin = replace(x = damageAmountCode,list = c(damageAmountCode != 0), values = 1)) # make a binary variable for damaged or not damaged

# load ozone indicator data
ozoneDat <- read.csv("../Data/OzoneIndicatorData/OzoneExposureIndexForVeg.csv")
```

When data were collected, data collectors recorded individuals with what they determined in the field to be ozone damage. We subsequently refer to these observations as "suspected ozone foliar injury." Field crews then collected a voucher specimen consisting of three leaves from three individuals for each species in a plot that had foliar injury. These voucher specimens were then sent to an expert for verification of the cause of foliar injury. That status (positive or negative for foliar injury) is then assigned to all individuals of that species in that plot that the field crew suspected had foliar injury). We refer to foliar injury data after confirmation by an expert as "confirmed ozone foliar injury." 
```{r}
# determine confirmed ozone foliar injury
datVerified <- read.csv("../Data/cleanedDataPkgFiles/CUPN_OzoneFoliarInjury_SpeciesLeafCollected_CLEANED.csv") |> 
  mutate(startDate = as_date(startDate)) |> 
  # add a column indicating that these leaves are sent to the specialist (were identified as ozone damaged in the field)
  mutate(damageAmountCode_bin = 1)
# i think you should be able to just join by site, date, plot, and species... 
datNew <- datAll |> 
  full_join(datVerified)

# now, make a new column in the datNew data frame that gives the "confirmed ozone foliar injury"
datNew <- datNew |> 
  mutate(confirmedOzoneInjury = ozoneInjuryReview) |> 
  mutate(confirmedOzoneInjury = replace(confirmedOzoneInjury, confirmedOzoneInjury == "Positive", 1), 
         confirmedOzoneInjury = replace(confirmedOzoneInjury, confirmedOzoneInjury == "Negative", 0), 
         confirmedOzoneInjury = replace(confirmedOzoneInjury, is.na(confirmedOzoneInjury), 0), 
         confirmedOzoneInjury = replace(confirmedOzoneInjury, confirmedOzoneInjury == "Inconclusive", 0.5))
```


Note that for the below plots, we only show information collected during "standard" plots (not "QA/QC") do avoid double-sampling of individuals. Later in this document we compare data collection across these two types of sampling to assess accuracy. 

# Exploratory figures

## Ozone Exposure Index for Vegetation
The Ozone exposure index for vegetation is the "3-month maximum 12-hour W126 index that occurs during the growing season (March–September), measured in parts per million-hours (ppm-hrs). The W126 index is a biologically relevant measure that preferentially weights the higher ozone concentrations more likely to cause plant damage." This definition and the ozone index values come from the NPS Air Quality in Parks [website](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/air/park-conditions-trends.htm). [NPS benchmarks](https://www.nps.gov/articles/air-analysis-methods-latest.htm#section_3.2), which are based on EPA standards from 2014, indicate that ozone exposure index values below 7.0 ppm-hrs are "good," values from 7.0-13.0 are "fair," and values >13.0 are "poor" 

There are yearly ozone index data collected on site for some park units. For others, there is an interpolated average index for each year, which interpolates values from nearby stations and then averages them over the previous five years (inclusive of the "current" year). For parks with on-site data collection, we also calculated a five year average index to allow us to compare values across all parks in the sampling protocol. 

::: {.callout-note collapse=true icon = false}
### Ozone exposure indices for vegetation across park units
```{r}
# get the yearly data
ozoneDat_yearly <- ozoneDat |> 
  filter(ozoneExposureIndexType == "yearly")

# calculate the 5-year moving average for each site
ozoneDat_yearlyTo5yr <- purrr::map(unique(ozoneDat_yearly$unitCode), .f = function(x) {
 ozoneDat_yearly |> 
    filter(unitCode == x) |>  
    mutate(
    movingAvgOzoneIndex = stats::filter(ts(ozoneExposureIndexForVegetation), filter = rep(1/5, 5), sides = 1  )
    ) 
} ) |> 
    purrr::list_c() |> 
  mutate(ozoneExposureIndexType = "average of previous 5 years inclusive of current year") |> 
  select(-ozoneExposureIndexForVegetation) |> 
  rename(ozoneExposureIndexForVegetation = movingAvgOzoneIndex) |> 
  select(names(ozoneDat))

# add back into the ozone data frame
ozoneDat <- ozoneDat |> 
  rbind(ozoneDat_yearlyTo5yr)

# make relevant info into ordered factors
ozoneDat <- ozoneDat |> 
  mutate(ozoneDataCollectionType = factor(ozoneDataCollectionType, ordered = TRUE, 
                                          levels = c("on-site sensor", "interpolated")),
         ozoneExposureIndexType = factor(ozoneExposureIndexType, ordered = TRUE, 
                                          levels = c("yearly", "average of previous 5 years inclusive of current year")))

# save plotting info as variables 
ozoneDataCollection_lu <- data.frame("ozoneDataCollectionType" = unique(ozoneDat$ozoneDataCollectionType), 
                              "ozoneDataCollectionType_shape" = factor(c(16, 17), ordered = TRUE))
ozoneExposure_lu <- data.frame( 
                              "ozoneExposureIndexType" = unique(ozoneDat$ozoneExposureIndexType), 
                              "ozoneExposureIndexType_color" = factor(c("#009900FF", "#990099FF"), ordered = TRUE), 
                              "ozoneExposureIndexType_plotName" = factor(c("Yearly", "Avg. over previous \n5 years"), ordered = TRUE))

ozoneDat <- ozoneDat |> 
  left_join(ozoneDataCollection_lu) |> 
  left_join(ozoneExposure_lu)

ribbonDat <- data.frame(
  "year" = c(2007, 2024, 2007, 2024, 2007, 2024), 
  "type" = factor(c("good","good", "fair", "fair","poor","poor"), 
                    levels = c("good", "fair", "poor")), 
  "ymin" = c(0, 0, 7, 7, 13, 13),
  "ymax" = c(7, 7, 13, 13, max(ozoneDat[ozoneDat$year >2006,"ozoneExposureIndexForVegetation"], na.rm = TRUE),max(ozoneDat[ozoneDat$year >2006,"ozoneExposureIndexForVegetation"], na.rm = TRUE))
)
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 10
#| fig-width: 8


# plot of number of individual plants w/ and without ozone by year across all park units
ozoneDat |>
  filter(year > 2006) |> 
  ggplot() +
  facet_wrap(~unitName, ncol = 2, axes = "all_x") +
  geom_ribbon(data = ribbonDat, aes(ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, x = year, fill = type)) + 
  scale_fill_discrete(palette = c("grey90", "grey80", "grey70"), name = "Ozone index \ncondition") +
  geom_line(aes(x = year, y = ozoneExposureIndexForVegetation, col = ozoneExposureIndexType))+
  geom_point(aes(x = year, y = ozoneExposureIndexForVegetation, col = ozoneExposureIndexType, pch = ozoneDataCollectionType)) + 
  xlim(2007, NA) + 
  scale_color_discrete(labels = as.character(unique(ozoneDat$ozoneExposureIndexType_plotName)) , name = "Index Type", palette = as.character(unique(ozoneDat$ozoneExposureIndexType_color)),
                       guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(pch = NA, linewidth = 1.5))) + 
  scale_shape_manual(name = "Source of Ozone Data", values = as.integer(as.character(unique(ozoneDat$ozoneDataCollectionType_shape)))) +
  labs(title = "Ozone exposure index for vegetation at CUPN parks during \nyears with foliar injury monitoring",
       x = "Year", y = "Ozone exposure index for vegetation, ppm-hrs") 
```
:::


## Ozone foliar injury rates
In the following figures, we show suspected and confirmed ozone foliar injury at all of the CUPN parks across the monitoring interval. We show the presence of foliar injury (i.e. number of individuals with and without injury) and the rate of foliar injury (i.e. proportion of total observed individuals with and without injury). We also show the presence and rate of ozone injury by severity. Each of these metrics is shown grouped across all parks and all species, groups across all parks by species, grouped across all species in a park, and by species in a park. 

## Presence and rate of *suspected* ozone foliar injury across all parks across time...

::: {.callout-note collapse=true icon = false}
### ... across all species
```{r}
# trim the data to only have observations from 'standard plots' (not QA/QC plots) 
datAll_std <- datNew |> 
  filter(eventType == "ozone standard") |> 
  mutate(confirmedOzoneInjury = factor(confirmedOzoneInjury, ordered = TRUE, levels = c(0, 1, 0.5))) |> 
  mutate(damageAmountCode_bin = factor(damageAmountCode_bin, ordered = TRUE, levels = c(0, 1, 0.5))) 


# plot of number of individual plants w/ and without ozone by year across all park units
datAll_std |> 
  ggplot() + 
  geom_bar(aes(x = as.integer(year), fill = as.factor(damageAmountCode_bin)), width = 0.9) + 
  guides(fill = guide_legend("Presence of \nOzone Foliar \nInjury")) + 
  theme(palette.fill.discrete = c("#332288", "#DDCC77", "#44AA99")) + 
  scale_fill_discrete(labels = c("No", "Yes", "Inconclusive")) + 
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Number of Individual Plants", 
        title = "Number of individual plants with and without suspected ozone \nfoliar injury, across all park units")+ 
     xlim(c(min(datAll$year)-1, max(datAll$year)+1))


# plot of proportion of individual plants w/ and without ozone by year across all park units
datAll_std |> 
  #group_by(year, damageAmountCode_bin) |> 
  #summarize(n = length(year))
  ggplot() + 
  geom_bar(aes(x = as.integer(year), fill = as.factor(damageAmountCode_bin)), position = "fill", width = 0.9) + 
  guides(fill = guide_legend("Presence of \nOzone Foliar \nInjury")) + 
  theme(palette.fill.discrete = c("#332288", "#DDCC77", "#44AA99")) + 
  scale_fill_discrete(labels = c("No", "Yes", "Inconclusive")) + 
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Proportion of sampled plants", 
        title = "Rate of suspected ozone \nfoliar injury, across all park units")+ 
     xlim(c(min(datAll$year)-1, max(datAll$year)+1))
```

```{r}
# make the damageSeverityCodeDescription column an ordered factor
datAll_std <- datAll_std |>
  mutate(damageSeverityCodeDescription = factor(damageSeverityCodeDescription, ordered = TRUE, levels = c("No Injury","1-6% of the leaf area of injured leaves has ozone symptoms", "7-25% of the leaf area of injured leaves has ozone symptoms" , "26-50% of the leaf area of injured leaves has ozone symptoms", "51-75% of the leaf area of injured leaves has ozone symptoms",  ">75% of the leaf area of injured leaves has ozone symptoms" ))) |>
  mutate(damageSeverityCodeDescription_confirmed = damageSeverityCodeDescription) |> # make new column for damageSeverityCodeDescription w/ correction for voucher classification
  mutate(damageSeverityCodeDescription_confirmed = replace(damageSeverityCodeDescription_confirmed, confirmedOzoneInjury == 0, "No Injury"),
         damageSeverityCodeDescription_confirmed = replace(damageSeverityCodeDescription_confirmed, confirmedOzoneInjury == 0.5, NA))


# make the damage severity code description have a column for color 
damSevColor_lu <- data.frame("damageSeverityCodeDescription" = unique(datAll_std$damageSeverityCodeDescription) |> sort(), 
                             "damageSeverityCodeDescription_color" = factor(c("#0F2B5FFF", "#5991C7FF","#8EC1E7FF", "#B9DBF1FF", "#D5A370FF", "#7B4F37FF"), ordered = TRUE, 
                                                                            levels = c("#0F2B5FFF", "#5991C7FF","#8EC1E7FF", "#B9DBF1FF", "#D5A370FF", "#7B4F37FF")), 
                             "damageSeverityCodeDescription_figNames" = factor(c("No Injury","1-6%","7-25%" ,"26-50%","51-75%",">75%"), 
                                                                               ordered = TRUE, 
                    levels = c("No Injury","1-6%","7-25%" ,"26-50%","51-75%",">75%")))
datAll_std <- 
  datAll_std |> 
  left_join(damSevColor_lu)


# plot of number of individual plants w/ and without ozone by year across all park units
datAll_std |>
  filter(!is.na(damageSeverityCodeDescription_confirmed)) |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(x = as.integer(year), fill = damageSeverityCodeDescription_confirmed), width = 0.9) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend("Percentage of leaf \narea or injured \nleaves with ozone \nsymptoms")) +
```

# Trend analysis

## Question 1: Is the presence of ozone foliar injury at all CUPN parks changing over the monitoring period?

### Considerations for this model
* Fitting a model like this across all parks does decrease our ability to estimate trends at each individual park, since the variation in the effect of year across parks is pooled and estimates for the year effect at each park are drawn toward the global mean estimate. However, with so many parks that do not have enough data to fit a model on their own, this approach allows us to at least do an exploratory analysis with all of the available data. 
* The response variable is presence or absence of ozone foliar injury (there isn't very much variation in severity of foliar injury -- the data are very zero inflated-- so we may need to use another structure for that model)
* We will use a binomial generalized linear mixed model, which is suitable for a binary response variable
* We will fit the model across all of the parks in order to maximize the amount of data available, and because we're interested in the trend across all CUPN parks
* we center the year variable, since the model will not converge with an un-transformed year variable
* Because the data are not independent (plots are visited repeatedly, and the park unit determines the years when plots are visited), we'll use *a random intercept for plot nested within park*. 
* We initially included a random slope for year according to the park intercept, but the resulting fit was singular due to the fact that the year random slope had low variance and was highly correlated with park. We also tried a random slope for year according to the nested random intercept for plot nested within park, but this model did not converge. 
* We include a *random intercept for year as a factor (year_f)* to account for year to year variation. Note that this is calculated as as.factor(centered year variable).
* We also expect that occurrence of foliar injury is different for different species due to differences in susceptibility. We also think that the trend in foliar injury is likely different across species. To help account for this, we include a *random intercept for species*
* I don't think the observations are temporally autocorrelated, because the presence of foliar injury in a previous year does not affect the presence of foliar injury in a subsequent year (leaves re-grow annually).
* The fact that plots aren't sampled every year in most parks is likely not problematic, since the presence/absence of data in a given year isn't related to ozone or other drivers (i.e. the data aren't "Missing Not at Random")
* This analysis makes the assumption that parks are assigned to panels randomly, and not using some other variable that may be confounding with ozone quantity or one of the predictors in the models.

This analysis was inspired in part by code from the forestTrends R package by Kate Miller, accessed 15 October, 2026
```{r, echo = FALSE}
# read in functions
source(file  = "../Functions/AnalysisFunctions.R")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse=true icon = false}
### Looking at variables to determine how to construct the model
```{r}
# format data correctly
datAll_std <- datAll_std |>
  mutate(confirmedOzoneInjury = as.numeric(as.character(confirmedOzoneInjury)))
# scale year
datAll_std <- datAll_std |>
  mutate(
         year_s = datawizard::standardize(year),
         year_f = as.factor(year_s))
# remove two observations with no year?
datAll_std <- datAll_std |>
  filter(!is.na(year))
# remove equivocal classifications, since they make it impossible to use the binomial distribution (also is not really meaningful from an analysis standpoint?)
datAll_std <- datAll_std |>
  filter(!is.na(confirmedOzoneInjury),
         confirmedOzoneInjury != 0.5)
unique(datAll_std$confirmedOzoneInjury)

# look at the response variable(presence/absence of injury) by year
datAll_std |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_density(aes(x = confirmedOzoneInjury, colour = year, group = year))

# look at the response variable(presence/absence of injury) by plot
datAll_std |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_density(aes(x = confirmedOzoneInjury, colour = siteName, group = siteName))


# look at the response variable(presence/absence of injury) by park unit
datAll_std |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_density(aes(x = confirmedOzoneInjury, colour = unitName, group = unitName))


# look at the response variable(presence/absence of injury) by species
datAll_std |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_density(aes(x = confirmedOzoneInjury, colour = scientificName, group = scientificName))

# is there a relationship between the response variable and year for different parks?
datAll_std |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_point(aes(y = jitter(confirmedOzoneInjury), x = year,
                 colour = unitName, group = unitName), alpha = .25) +
  geom_smooth(aes(y = jitter(confirmedOzoneInjury), x = year,
                 colour = unitName, group = unitName),  method = "glm")

# is there a relationship between the park name and year of data collection? (due to panel design?) -- yes
datAll_std |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = year, y = unitName), alpha = .25)
anova(lm(year ~ unitName, data = datAll_std))

# is there a relationship between the plot name and year of data collection? (due to panel design?) -- yes
datAll_std |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = year, y = siteName), alpha = .25)
anova(lm(year ~ siteName, data = datAll_std))

## both of the above results are why having a random effect for site (or at least for year) in the model should be helpful

## we also know that different parks have different species, so having a random effect for species will help address that correlation
## how many plots are in each park?
table(datAll_std |> select(siteName, unitName) |> unique() |> select(unitName))

## how many species are in a park?
table(datAll_std |> select(unitName, scientificName) |> unique() |> select(unitName))

## how many species are in a site?
table(datAll_std |> select(siteName, scientificName) |> unique() |> select(siteName))

## there are not nearly enough observations to include a random effect for species (there are multiple species that have only a few (~2) observations)
table(datAll_std |> select(scientificName))
```
:::

### Fit a generalized linear mixed model with a random effect for plot name and a random effect for species.
<!-- However, a model with the full dataset does not converge, likely because there are quite a few species for which there are only a few observations. In this model, we've removed species for which we have fewer than 20 observations -->
```{r}
# random effect for site and random effect for species (there is variation in the starting amount of foliar injury, and the change in rate of foliar injury over time is different for each species at each site )
# try setting REML to "true" ()
mod1 <- glmer(data = datAll_std, formula = confirmedOzoneInjury ~ year_s  + (1|year_f)
              + (1|scientificName) + (1|unitName/siteName), family = binomial(link = "logit"), control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa"))

summary(mod1)

```

### Look at patterns in simulated residuals
(we use conditional residuals, which allow us to look at patterns in the random effects. We already know that the random effect variables are driving patterns in the response (why we include them as random effects in the first place) so we expect to see patterns in the unconditional/marginal residuals)
We use the DHARMa R package to simulate scaled residuals ("a scaled residual value of 0.5 means that half of the simulated data are higher than the observed rate, half of them lower." -- from the DHARMa vignette). A well specified model will have scaled residuals with a uniform (flat) distribution, and will not show a directional relationship when plotted against model predictors.
```{r}

# use the DHARMa package to simulate residuals and and plot the results
mod1_resids <- DHARMa::simulateResiduals(mod1,
                                 response = TRUE, #for models with integer response
                                 simulateREs = "conditional" # re-simulates both random and fixed effects
                                 )
plot(mod1_resids)

# plot residuals against year
plotResiduals(mod1_resids, form = ~year_s)

# plot residuals against year as a factor
plotResiduals(mod1_resids, form = ~year_f)

# plot residuals against species
plotResiduals(mod1_resids, form= ~scientificName)
# plot residuals against plot
plotResiduals(mod1_resids, form= ~siteName, )
# plot residuals against park
plotResiduals(mod1_resids, form= ~unitName)

# look at the dispersion of the model
testDispersion(mod1_resids, plot = TRUE)

# look at the dispersion of the model according to species
testDispersion(recalculateResiduals(mod1_resids, group = ~scientificName), plot = TRUE)

# look at the dispersion of the model according to plot
testDispersion(recalculateResiduals(mod1_resids, group = ~siteName), plot = TRUE)

# look at the dispersion of the model according to park
testDispersion(recalculateResiduals(mod1_resids, group = ~unitName), plot = TRUE)

## what is the correlation between the random effect terms? what is the standard deviation?
VarCorr(mod1) |> as.data.frame()
```

There is a slightly significant KS test, which indicates that the data are perhaps not an ideal fit to the statistical distribution used in the model. The residuals do not have a significant pattern of variation across year, but there is some significant variation across park. However, the model does not appear to be over-dispersed.
The standard deviations of the random effects aren't too close to zero, so the data are currently supporting the random effect.



### Are the random effects correlated with the predictor (year?) 
A correlation would indicate that the random effects are absorbing some of the effects of the fixed effect structure, which would indicate that the fixed effect structure was poorly specified. 
```{r}

     y = 3)


# is the site random effect correlated with the predictor?

plot(mod1_ranEf$siteName$`(Intercept)` ~ y2$year_s, xlab = "mean value of year (scaled) for each level of the site random effect", ylab = "ran. intercept for each level of the site ran. eff.",  main = "Correlation of site random effect with year")
```

### Model coefficients and confidence intervals
We show bootstrap percentile confidence intervals for fixed effects, which are calculated using the lme4::confint() function
```{r}
mod_df <- broom.mixed::tidy(mod1) |>
  dplyr::filter(effect == 'fixed') |>
      dplyr::select(term, estimate) |> data.frame()

new_df <- data.frame("year_s" = sort(unique(mod1@frame$year_s)))
pred_df <- data.frame(term = paste0(substr("year_s", 1, 1), new_df[,"year_s"], "_response"),
                          estimate = stats::predict(mod1, newdata = new_df,
                                                    type = 'response', re.form = NA))

## see if the confidence intervals have been saved yet 
if(sum(c("fixefCI.rds") %in% list.files("../Data/intermediateDataFiles/model1_CIs/")) == 0) {
 fixefCI <- confint(mod1, parm = "beta_", method = "boot", nsim = 500,
        boot.type = "perc", parallel = "multicore", ncpus = 4)
saveRDS(fixefCI, "../Data/intermediateDataFiles/model1_CIs/fixefCI.rds")
} else {
  #mod1CI_year_s <- readRDS("../Data/intermediateDataFiles/model1_CIs/year_s_CI.rds")
  fixefCI <- readRDS("../Data/intermediateDataFiles/model1_CIs/fixefCI.rds")
}
  
  


# plot the fixed effect coefficients
 broom.mixed::tidy(mod1, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE)  |>
   filter(effect == "fixed") |> 
   select(-conf.low, -conf.high) |> 
   left_join(data.frame("term" = c("(Intercept)", "year_s"), "conf.low" = c(fixefCI[,1]), 
                        "conf.high" = fixefCI[,2])) |> 
   #transform(term=sprintf("%s.%s", term)) |>
   mutate(model = "mod1",
          crossesZero = "no") |>
   mutate(crossesZero = replace(crossesZero, conf.high > 0  & conf.low < 0, "yes")) |> 
   ggplot() + 
   geom_vline(aes(xintercept = 0), linetype = 2) + 
   geom_point(aes(x = estimate, y = term, col = crossesZero)) + 
   geom_segment(aes(y = term, x = conf.high, xend = conf.low, col = crossesZero)) + 
   labs(title = "Fixed effect coefficients and bootstrap CIs from the model: \nfoliarInjury ~ year_s + (1|year_f) + (1|species) + (1|plot/park)", x = "Estimate", y = "Model Term") + 
   scale_color_discrete(name = "CI crosses zero?")
```
### Show population-level predictions 
(These are unconditional predictions, which are predictions for a 'typical' park/plot/species) with parametric bootstrap confidence intervals
```{r}
# set up the prediction data.frame
yr_mean <- mean(datAll_std$year); yr_sd <- sd(datAll_std$year)   # from the UNSCALED year variable from the data frame used to fit the model, so that the scalign factors are the same here as they were for creating the year_s variable used ot fit the model

newDat <- data.frame(year = seq(min(datAll_std$year), max(datAll_std$year), length.out = 50))
newDat$year_s <- (newDat$year - yr_mean) / yr_sd

# generate predictions (w/ all intercepts at their mean)
newDat$pred <- predict(mod1, newdata = newDat, re.form = NA, type = "response")

# now, calculate CIs 
predFun <- function(m) predict(m, newdata = newDat,type = "response")

# get 95% confidence interval 
## see if the bootstrap confidence intervals have been saved yet 
if(sum(c("predBootCIs.rds") %in% list.files("../Data/intermediateDataFiles/model1_CIs/")) == 0) {

    boot <-  bootMer(mod1, predFun, nsim = 100, re.form = NA)
saveRDS(boot, "../Data/intermediateDataFiles/model1_CIs/predBootCIs.rds")
} else {
  #mod1CI_year_s <- readRDS("../Data/intermediateDataFiles/model1_CIs/year_s_CI.rds")
  boot <- readRDS("../Data/intermediateDataFiles/model1_CIs/predBootCIs.rds")
}

newDat <- newDat |> 
  cbind(confint(boot))

#plot
ggplot(newDat) + 
  geom_ribbon(aes(x = year, ymin = `2.5 %`, ymax = `97.5 %`), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line(aes(x = year, y = pred)) + 
  labs(y = "P(ozone foliar injury)", title = "Predictions of ozone foliar injury for a 'typical' park, plot, and species", 
       subtitle = "95% parametric bootstrap confidence interval shown in grey")

```

### Show predictions from this cross-park model for individual park units 
(These are predictions for a typical plot and species in that park, with random effects for everything except for park held fixed) with parametric bootstrap confidence intervals. Note that these CI estimates ignore uncertainty in the park-level intercepts themselves, so these CIs are the lower bound of uncertainty.  
```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 18
# set up the prediction data.frame

newDat2 <- expand.grid(
  year = seq(min(datAll_std$year), max(datAll_std$year), length.out = 50),
  unitName = unique(datAll_std$unitName)
)

newDat2$year_s <- (newDat2$year - yr_mean) / yr_sd
# add values for other effects that we don't allow to vary in this version of prediction

newDat2$year_s         <- (newDat2$year - yr_mean) / yr_sd
newDat2$siteName       <- datAll_std$siteName[1]
newDat2$scientificName <- datAll_std$scientificName[1]
newDat2$year_f         <- datAll_std$year_f[1]

# generate predictions (w/ all intercepts at their mean)
newDat2$pred <- predict(mod1, newdata = newDat2, re.form = ~(1|unitName), type = "response")

# now, calculate CIs 
predFun2 <- function(m) predict(m, newdata = newDat2, type = "response", allow.new.levels = TRUE,)

# get 95% confidence interval 
## see if the bootstrap confidence intervals have been saved yet 
if(sum(c("predBootCIs_perPark.rds") %in% list.files("../Data/intermediateDataFiles/model1_CIs/")) == 0) {

    boot_perPark <-  bootMer(mod1, predFun2, nsim = 100, re.form = ~(1|unitName), use.u = TRUE)
saveRDS(boot_perPark, "../Data/intermediateDataFiles/model1_CIs/predBootCIs_perPark.rds")
} else {
  #mod1CI_year_s <- readRDS("../Data/intermediateDataFiles/model1_CIs/year_s_CI.rds")
  boot_perPark <- readRDS("../Data/intermediateDataFiles/model1_CIs/predBootCIs_perPark.rds")
}

newDat2 <- newDat2 |> 
  cbind(confint(boot_perPark))

#plot
ggplot(newDat2) + 
  facet_wrap(~unitName, ncol = 2) + 
  #geom_point(data = datAll_std, aes(x = year, y = jitter(confirmedOzoneInjury))) + 
  geom_ribbon(aes(x = year, ymin = `2.5 %`, ymax = `97.5 %`), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line(aes(x = year, y = pred)) + 
  labs(y = "P(ozone foliar injury)", title = "Predictions of ozone foliar injury for a 'typical' park, plot, and species", 
       subtitle = "95% parametric bootstrap confidence interval shown in grey")

```

### Interpretive takeaways
* When looking across all parks collectively, there is a negative trend in the presence of confirmed ozone foliar injury across the study period, although the effect is not significant (the CI of the year estimate crosses zero). 
* There are different degrees of decrease (i.e. the y-intercept of the trend is different) in the presence of confirmed ozone foliar injury when we look at the park-level effects, although these effects are shrunken toward the mean effect across all parks due to the model structure. The data could not support a model with a random intercept for year, which would have allowed for different *rates* of change across parks rather than just different intercepts for the trend across parks. 

## Question 2: Is the presence of ozone foliar injury at each CUPN park changing over time? 

### Considerations: 
* We do not have adequate data to fit models for many parks, particularly for those parks that only have two visits or that have no observations of confirmed foliar injury. 
* For those parks that do have a 



### Fit a generalized linear mixed model with a random effect for plot name and a random effect for species.
<!-- However, a model with the full dataset does not converge, likely because there are quite a few species for which there are only a few observations. In this model, we've removed species for which we have fewer than 20 observations -->
```{r}
# random effect for site and random effect for species (there is variation in the starting amount of foliar injury, and the change in rate of foliar injury over time is different for each species at each site )
# try setting REML to "true" ()
mod2 <- glmer(data = datAll_std, formula = confirmedOzoneInjury ~ year_s*unitName  + (1|year_f)
              + (1|scientificName) + (1|unitName:siteName), family = binomial(link = "logit"), control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa"))

summary(mod2)

```

### Look at patterns in simulated residuals
(we use conditional residuals, which allow us to look at patterns in the random effects. We already know that the random effect variables are driving patterns in the response (why we include them as random effects in the first place) so we expect to see patterns in the unconditional/marginal residuals)
We use the DHARMa R package to simulate scaled residuals ("a scaled residual value of 0.5 means that half of the simulated data are higher than the observed rate, half of them lower." -- from the DHARMa vignette). A well specified model will have scaled residuals with a uniform (flat) distribution, and will not show a directional relationship when plotted against model predictors.
```{r}

# use the DHARMa package to simulate residuals and and plot the results
mod2_resids <- DHARMa::simulateResiduals(mod2,
                                 response = TRUE, #for models with integer response
                                 simulateREs = "conditional" # re-simulates both random and fixed effects
                                 )
plot(mod2_resids)

# plot residuals against year
plotResiduals(mod2_resids, form = ~year_s)

# plot residuals against year as a factor
plotResiduals(mod2_resids, form = ~year_f)

# plot residuals against species
plotResiduals(mod2_resids, form= ~scientificName)
# plot residuals against plot
plotResiduals(mod2_resids, form= ~siteName, )
# plot residuals against park
plotResiduals(mod2_resids, form= ~unitName)

# look at the dispersion of the model
testDispersion(mod2_resids, plot = TRUE)

# look at the dispersion of the model according to species
testDispersion(recalculateResiduals(mod2_resids, group = ~scientificName), plot = TRUE)

# look at the dispersion of the model according to plot
testDispersion(recalculateResiduals(mod2_resids, group = ~siteName), plot = TRUE)

# look at the dispersion of the model according to park
testDispersion(recalculateResiduals(mod2_resids, group = ~unitName), plot = TRUE)

## what is the correlation between the random effect terms? what is the standard deviation?
VarCorr(mod2) |> as.data.frame()
```

There is a slightly significant KS test, which indicates that the data are perhaps not an ideal fit to the statistical distribution used in the model. The residuals do not have a significant pattern of variation across year, but there is some significant variation across park. However, the model does not appear to be over-dispersed.
The standard deviations of the random effects aren't too close to zero, so the data are currently supporting the random effect.

```{r}
newDat$year_s <- (newDat$year - yr_mean) / yr_sd

# generate predictions (w/ all intercepts at their mean)
newDat$pred <- predict(mod2, newdata = newDat, re.form = NA, type = "response")

# now, calculate CIs 
predFun <- function(m) predict(m, newdata = newDat,type = "response")

# get 95% confidence interval 
## see if the bootstrap confidence intervals have been saved yet 
if(sum(c("predBootCIs.rds") %in% list.files("../Data/intermediateDataFiles/model1_CIs/")) == 0) {

    boot <-  bootMer(mod2, predFun, nsim = 100, re.form = NA)
saveRDS(boot, "../Data/intermediateDataFiles/model1_CIs/predBootCIs.rds")
} else {
  #mod2CI_year_s <- readRDS("../Data/intermediateDataFiles/model1_CIs/year_s_CI.rds")
  boot <- readRDS("../Data/intermediateDataFiles/model1_CIs/predBootCIs.rds")
}

newDat <- newDat |> 
  cbind(confint(boot))

#plot
ggplot(newDat) + 
  geom_ribbon(aes(x = year, ymin = `2.5 %`, ymax = `97.5 %`), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line(aes(x = year, y = pred)) + 
  labs(y = "P(ozone foliar injury)", title = "Predictions of ozone foliar injury for a 'typical' park, plot, and species", 
       subtitle = "95% parametric bootstrap confidence interval shown in grey")

```

### Show predictions from this cross-park model for individual park units 
(These are predictions for a typical plot and species in that park, with random effects for everything except for park held fixed) with parametric bootstrap confidence intervals. Note that these CI estimates ignore uncertainty in the park-level intercepts themselves, so these CIs are the lower bound of uncertainty.  
```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 18
# set up the prediction data.frame

newDat2 <- expand.grid(
  year = seq(min(datAll_std$year), max(datAll_std$year), length.out = 50),
  unitName = unique(datAll_std$unitName)
)

newDat2$year_s <- (newDat2$year - yr_mean) / yr_sd
# add values for other effects that we don't allow to vary in this version of prediction

newDat2$year_s         <- (newDat2$year - yr_mean) / yr_sd
newDat2$siteName       <- datAll_std$siteName[1]
newDat2$scientificName <- datAll_std$scientificName[1]
newDat2$year_f         <- datAll_std$year_f[1]

# generate predictions (w/ all intercepts at their mean)
newDat2$pred <- predict(mod2, newdata = newDat2, re.form = ~(1|unitName), type = "response")

# now, calculate CIs 
predFun2 <- function(m) predict(m, newdata = newDat2, type = "response", allow.new.levels = TRUE,)

# get 95% confidence interval 
## see if the bootstrap confidence intervals have been saved yet 
if(sum(c("predBootCIs_perPark.rds") %in% list.files("../Data/intermediateDataFiles/model1_CIs/")) == 0) {

    boot_perPark <-  bootMer(mod2, predFun2, nsim = 100, re.form = ~(1|unitName), use.u = TRUE)
saveRDS(boot_perPark, "../Data/intermediateDataFiles/model1_CIs/predBootCIs_perPark.rds")
} else {
  #mod2CI_year_s <- readRDS("../Data/intermediateDataFiles/model1_CIs/year_s_CI.rds")
  boot_perPark <- readRDS("../Data/intermediateDataFiles/model1_CIs/predBootCIs_perPark.rds")
}

newDat2 <- newDat2 |> 
  cbind(confint(boot_perPark))

#plot
ggplot(newDat2) + 
  facet_wrap(~unitName, ncol = 2) + 
  #geom_point(data = datAll_std, aes(x = year, y = jitter(confirmedOzoneInjury))) + 
  geom_ribbon(aes(x = year, ymin = `2.5 %`, ymax = `97.5 %`), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line(aes(x = year, y = pred)) + 
  labs(y = "P(ozone foliar injury)", title = "Predictions of ozone foliar injury for a 'typical' park, plot, and species", 
       subtitle = "95% parametric bootstrap confidence interval shown in grey")

```
